chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: The missing diamond ring and his girlfriend's family
summary: Rex blamed him for a lost ring that his girlfriend's son had taken; he describes her family.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. So he had charge of the units and his own apartment free. So I went over there one night and I took my girl friend's sons over with me at that particular time. And Rex comes up missing his diamond ring. And for a long time he accused me of taking his diamond ring, but he never said anything to me about it, whereas the oldest son is the one that got the diamond ring. And he's still a criminal. He's in the penitentiary now. Grew up, you know, in
nothing but institutions. And I guess he's institutionalized now. Today I was talking to his mother and grandmother today, and he's started a music program up there.
This is the son of your girl friend at that time.

Yeah. The older son. And she had four kids, two daughters and two sons. And I had met her mother and father in Denver when I was with Louis Armstrong, and she was just about seven years old at that time. I had her on my knee. I said, 'You pretty little thing, I'm going to wait on you.' And she didn't forget it, but I had forgotten all about it. So one night she asked me -- well, I was going with her roomer, and she was quite large, and I knew she was a woman. I find out later she's 17 years old. And I shivered all over. San Quentin quail. So --
